title: Protocol to extract and measure ubiquinone and rhodoquinone in murine tissues
author: Jerome, Spinelli
materials: This step prepares the samples to be run on an LC-MS method to detect and measure non-polar metabolites. Keeping the samples in an autosampler held at 4 degrees C prevents the degradation of the metabolites during the run.46.Place the dried down samples on ice (not dry ice).47.Add the appropriate amount of the LC-MS resuspension buffer to achieve 20 μg/μL based on the protein quantifications done in step 35.48.Vortex the samples for 10 minutes at 4 degrees C in a cold room.49.Pipette 20 μL of each sample into an autosampler vial.CRITICAL: The volume to aliquot into autosampler vials can vary depending on injection needle offset parameters of the LC-MS setup. We recommend putting at least 20 μL volume in each vial, but higher volumes will also work. Be sure there are no bubbles in the autosampler vial to avoid injecting air instead of sample.50.The samples should be kept on regular ice while you set up the LC-MS for the run.51.It is recommended if you are running different tissues in the same run, to put at least one extraction solvent blank in between them. We recommend that LC-MS data is analyzed using Tracefinder 5.1 SP1 (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Peaks should be integrated according to a stringent 5 ppm mass tolerance and minimal shifts in retention time compared to standards. The area under the curve for all adduct integrations should be summed together to get a total abundance of RQ and UQ, respectively. The peak areas for UQ and RQ can be integrated simultaneously on tissues processed together on the LC-MS. These values do not need to be normalized because samples should be loaded into the LC-MS with even protein quantifications. The ion counts of ubiquinone and rhodoquinone cannot be compared unless standard curves for each of these metabolites have been run and absolute quantification is performed.

steps.title: Label tubes and prepare buffers
steps.instruction: Label four sets of 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes and two sets of 2 mL tubes. Prepare mitochondria isolation buffer and pre‑cool at 4 °C. Make a 1X RIPA buffer stock, keep on ice and store at –20 °C when not in use (RIPA is only for protein quantification, never contacts LC‑MS samples). Prepare extraction buffers: acidified LC‑MS grade methanol and LC‑MS grade hexane, pre‑cool at 4 °C, using only glassware that has never been exposed to detergent and washed with ultrapure water. Make LC mobile phase solvents A and B right before use.

steps.title: Cool and thaw isolation buffer
steps.instruction: If stored at –20 °C, thaw the isolation buffer in a 37 °C water bath only until ice disappears, then shake to mix and place on regular ice.

steps.title: Prepare homogenizer on ice
steps.instruction: Place a glass homogenizer and pestle on regular ice, burying the bottom portion in the ice to keep them cold.

steps.title: Thaw tissue aliquots
steps.instruction: Thaw mouse tissue aliquots on regular ice (5–10 min).

steps.title: Add isolation buffer to tissue
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL isolation buffer to the tube containing tissue powder, invert 2–3 times, then pour into the homogenizer. Add another 1 mL isolation buffer to a 2 mL tube, invert once, and pour into the homogenizer. Do not vortex.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue
steps.instruction: With the homogenizer submerged in ice, move the pestle up and down slowly for 30 strokes, avoiding air bubbles and never lifting the pestle above the liquid surface.

steps.title: Collect homogenate and clean homogenizer
steps.instruction: Pour the homogenate into a new 2 mL microcentrifuge tube. Rinse the homogenizer and pestle in deionized water, flick to remove excess water, and dry completely before the next sample.

steps.title: Repeat homogenization for all samples
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 5–7 for each tissue sample.

steps.title: First centrifugation to remove debris
steps.instruction: Spin the tubes in a refrigerated centrifuge at 600 × g, 4 °C for 10 min. The pellet (cell debris and nuclei) is discarded; the cloudy supernatant contains mitochondria.

steps.title: Transfer mitochondrial supernatant
steps.instruction: Using a p1000 pipette, transfer the supernatant 1 mL at a time to a new 2 mL tube, being careful not to disturb the pellet. Discard the original tube.

steps.title: Second centrifugation to pellet mitochondria
steps.instruction: Spin the transferred supernatant at 7,000 × g, 4 °C for 10 min. A brown mitochondrial pellet forms.

steps.title: Discard supernatant and wash mitochondria
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant in 1 mL increments with a p1000 pipette. Resuspend the pellet in 2 mL isolation buffer by pipetting up and down. Spin again at 7,000 × g, 4 °C for 10 min. Discard the supernatant in 1 mL increments. Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL isolation buffer.

steps.title: Aliquot for protein quantification
steps.instruction: Transfer 25 µL of the resuspended mitochondria to a new 1.5 mL tube for later protein quantification; the remaining 975 µL stays in the 2 mL tube for quinone extraction.

steps.title: Final spin and store pellets
steps.instruction: Spin all tubes at 7,000 × g, 4 °C for 10 min. Discard all supernatant, leaving a brown crude mitochondrial pellet. Store the pellets at –80 °C until extraction.

steps.title: Non‑polar metabolite extraction
steps.instruction: Place the mitochondria tubes on dry ice. Cool acidified LC‑MS methanol and LC‑MS hexane on dry ice. Add 500 µL acidified methanol to each tube, vortex 15 min at 4 °C in a cold room. Bring tubes to a chemical fume hood, add 500 µL hexane, vortex 15 min at 4 °C. Centrifuge at 21,300 × g (or top speed) at 4 °C for 10 min to separate layers. Transfer the top hexane layer to a new 1.5 mL tube with a p1000 pipette; discard the rest. Dry the hexane layer in a refrigerated speedvac (‑4 °C to 4 °C, cold trap ‑105 °C) until no liquid remains (1–4 h). If a speedvac is unavailable, use a nitrogen evaporator. Pause point: dried tubes may be stored at –80 °C if drying is delayed.

steps.title: Resuspend dried extracts
steps.instruction: Place dried samples on ice (not dry ice). Add LC‑MS resuspension buffer to achieve 20 µg/µL based on the protein amount measured in step 13. Vortex 10 min at 4 °C. Pipette 20 µL of each sample into labeled autosampler vials (ensure no bubbles) and keep vials on ice, covered with aluminum foil.

steps.title: Prepare LC‑MS run
steps.instruction: Label autosampler vials and keep covered with foil. Include 2–3 blanks (resuspension buffer) at the start, a mock injection, then samples (grouped by tissue type or random) with an extraction‑solvent blank between tissue subtypes. Optionally add QC pools or RQ standards. End the run with 2–3 blanks. Use a Luna 3 µm PFP(2) 100 Å, 100 × 2 mm column (Phenomenex). Prepare mobile phase solvents A and B. Set gradient: hold 70 % B for 0–3 min, increase to 98 % B over 0.25 min, hold 98 % B for 1.75 min, increase to 99 % B over 1 min, hold 99 % B for 2.75 min, decrease to 70 % B over 1.75 min, hold 70 % B for 2 min. Flow rate 0.5 mL/min.

steps.title: Run full‑scan MS
steps.instruction: Inject 2 µL of each sample. MS settings: full scan, m/z 600–1000, positive ion mode, spray voltage 4.0 kV, heated capillary temperature 320 °C, C‑ESI probe temperature 30 °C, sheath gas 40 (room temp), auxiliary gas 15 (room temp), sweep gas 1 (room temp), resolution 17,500, AGC target 3 × 10⁶, maximum injection time 250 ms.

steps.title: Optional SIM for RQ detection
steps.instruction: Set up a SIM method with the same source parameters as the full scan. Target m/z values: RQ‑9 [H⁺] 780.6289, RQ‑9 [Na⁺] 802.61087, RQH₂‑9 [H⁺] 782.64457, RQH₂‑9 [Na⁺] 804.62652, RQ‑10 [H⁺] 848.69152, RQ‑10 [Na⁺] 870.67347, RQH₂‑10 [H⁺] 850.70717, RQH₂‑10 [Na⁺] 872.68912. Inject 2 µL.

steps.title: MS/MS PRM confirmation
steps.instruction: Configure a PRM method: positive mode, spray voltage 4.0 kV, capillary 320 °C, probe 30 °C, sheath gas 40, auxiliary gas 15, sweep gas 1, resolution 17,500, AGC target 2 × 10⁵, max injection time 250 ms, isolation window 0.5 m/z, stepped NCE 30. Monitor: RQ‑9 [H⁺] 780.6289 (4–6 min), RQH₂‑9 [H⁺] 782.6445 (4–6 min), UQ‑9 [H⁺] 795.6285 (5–7 min), UQH₂‑9 [H⁺] 797.6442 (5–7 min). Inject 2 µL of each sample.

steps.title: Analyze LC‑MS data
steps.instruction: After the run, process data in Tracefinder 5.1 SP1 (Thermo Fisher). Integrate peaks with a 5 ppm mass tolerance, sum all adduct areas to obtain total UQ and RQ abundances. No additional protein normalization is required because samples were loaded with equal protein. Absolute quantification requires standard curves for each metabolite.
